answer: A $60 audit deposit stands behind every identity in the orchard, refundable only after it passes. Each epoch a public lottery draws 8% of identities off the mesa for a deep audit, and three rotating auditors run the checks that week. A failed audit burns the deposit and piles a fine into a dune that doubles with each extra clone caught from the same operator in one sweep, $150 then $300 then $600. One sweep catching 12 clones costs $614,250 in fines plus $720 in lost deposits, against $60 for one honest agent. Planting fakes here is watering a field that charges rent by the row.
